*Figure 17.4: Functions sampled from a GP using various stationary periodic kernels. Generated by gpKernelPlot.m.*

For values ν ∈ {½, 3/2, 5/2}, the function simplifies as follows:

𝒦(r; ½, ℓ) = exp(-r/ℓ)  (17.20)
𝒦(r; 3/2, ℓ) = (1 + √3 r/ℓ) exp(-√3 r/ℓ)  (17.21)
𝒦(r; 5/2, ℓ) = (1 + √5 r/ℓ + 5 r²/(3 ℓ²)) exp(-√5 r/ℓ)  (17.22)

The value ν = ½ corresponds to the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process, which describes the velocity of a particle undergoing Brownian motion. The corresponding function is continuous but not differentiable, and hence is very “jagged”. See Fig. 17.3b for an illustration.
